findings.claim: Snapshot installation can leave an open SurrealDB transaction on any mid-snapshot error, so the advertised atomic snapshot/checkpoint seam is not reliably cleaned up.
findings.evidence: In `install_projection_snapshot`, a transaction is begun, then `delete`, per-entity `EntityRow::from_change`, `upsert`, cursor `upsert`, and `commit` all use `?` without a cancellation path; by contrast `apply_projection` explicitly calls `transaction.cancel().await` on both duplicate and error branches. Acceptance criterion 2 requires a durable population/checkpoint seam and snapshot-to-WAL catch-up.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the snapshot transaction body like `apply_projection`: collect the result, call `transaction.cancel().await` before returning any error, and only return success after `commit` succeeds.

findings.claim: A revoked watch is only detected after the underlying entity stream yields another item, so an idle watch can remain open indefinitely after authorization is revoked.
findings.evidence: The watch guard performs `authz.check(&view_tuple).await` only inside `stream.then(...)` after an item arrives, and the outer `unfold` awaits `checked.as_mut().next().await?`; no independent revocation signal or periodic recheck exists. The completion receipt claims the correction makes a revoked watch terminate on its next poll without waiting for another event from an idle underlying source.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an authorization-revocation signal or periodic/explicit recheck path that can yield `PermissionDenied` even when the underlying entity stream is pending, or narrow the documented claim to per-event reauthorization only.
